requirement.original: Who killed session processes this morning when user archived?
requirement.clarified: Forensic investigation of the 2026-04-08 09:05 UTC session cascade triggered by archiving session 1140deaf
requirement.what: Root cause analysis of session cascade incident
requirement.why: Understanding whether the app, daemon, or watcher caused the mass session kill

included: Identification of each actor in the cascade chain

success_criteria: Complete timeline from trigger to cascade
Explanation of why 17:50 archive did not cascade

root_cause_analysis.symptom: Archiving one session at 09:05 UTC killed ALL sessions across all daemons
root_cause_analysis.root_cause: Three-actor chain: (1) App sent killSession RPC which correctly killed the archived session process. (2) Daemon detected dead PID and removed it from session_dirs.txt. (3) Session watcher (OLD code before Bug #61 fix) detected the session count decrease, treated it as a crash event, and executed blanket orphan-kill + mass-respawn across ALL daemons.
root_cause_analysis.root_cause_commit: N/A - the old watcher behavior was the root cause, already fixed by Bug #61
root_cause_analysis.why_introduced: The watcher was designed to recover from daemon crashes where ALL sessions die. It treated ANY session disappearance as a potential crash and did a full restore.
root_cause_analysis.why_problematic: A single intentional session kill (user archive) triggered the same full-restore path as a daemon crash. The blanket orphan-kill killed all healthy sessions, then respawned them all, causing multiple secondary cascades.

context.codebase_state: Bug #61 fix already applied to session recovery script
context.recent_commits: 79cf62b5 fix: Bug #61 -- scope session recovery per-daemon

forensic_timeline.09:04:32.874: App sends killSession RPC to session cmnpqnr9e124rt615ig4jwdw1 (PID 289607, claude session 1140deaf)
forensic_timeline.09:04:32.875: CLI process receives killSession, calls killThisHappy(), begins cleanup
forensic_timeline.09:04:32.882: CLI process cleanup complete, process exits
forensic_timeline.09:05:26.388: Daemon health check detects PID 289607 no longer exists, removes from tracking
forensic_timeline.09:05:26.000: Watcher detects session count drop (15->14), triggers auto-restore
forensic_timeline.09:05:39-42: Watcher kills 6 healthy session processes as 'orphans' for /root/.happy
forensic_timeline.09:06:41-57: Watcher kills 3 jade sessions as 'orphans', respawns them
forensic_timeline.09:07:02-05: Watcher kills 1 dev session, respawns it
forensic_timeline.09:09:11: Another session dies during respawn chaos, triggers THIRD cascade (but lock prevents concurrent restore)

key_findings.who_killed_pid_289607: The APP via killSession RPC. This is the INTENDED behavior for archive.
key_findings.who_caused_the_cascade: The SESSION WATCHER (old code). It treated a single session disappearance as a full crash event and did blanket kill + respawn.
key_findings.why_17_50_did_not_cascade: Bug #61 fix was applied before the 17:50 test. The new watcher does not blanket-kill on single session disappearance.

development_approach.strategy: No implementation needed - this is a completed investigation. Bug #61 fix already resolved the cascade issue.
development_approach.validation_approach: The 17:50 archive test confirmed the fix works: 39 processes before, 39 after (minus the archived one).

research_findings.reason: Forensic investigation of specific incident using log analysis, not a design or architecture question
